=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** The Seller's cover note and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA text, the data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012), or our DD reports. Clause references follow the Seller's numbering. NSW counsel should confirm the positions below before they go into the mark-up.

---

## 1. The overall picture

The cover note says the package is "fair and balanced". Read with the Disclosure Letter, it is not. Three mechanisms work together to empty out the buyer's protection:

1. **Disclosure of the whole data room and public records** (DL 1.1–1.2).
2. **No claim for anything the Buyer "or its advisers" knew or could have discovered** (cl 8.3).
3. **All limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5), including title, tax, indemnities and, on its face, fraud.

Together, almost every risk we have identified would be disclosed, known, or capped at 20%, and time-barred after 18 months.

The cover note also describes several issues in more comfortable terms than the Seller's own Disclosure Letter does:

| Issue | Cover note says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | No final written consent; 11.3 conditions not evidenced (DL 2) |
| Riverlark | release "following Completion" | Not repaid; no discharge (DL 3) |
| Ironquay | indemnity "adequate" | AUD 180k open; no confirmatory assignment (DL 4) |
| DD-006 incident | "not expected to be material" | Scope, access and notification all unknown (DL 6) |
| Sandbar | "ordinary course" | DL expressly does *not* say ordinary course, unavoidable or terminable (DL 8) |

DL 11 states that no conclusion is expressed. We should treat the cover note as advocacy and rely only on the DL and our own diligence.

**Dating point:** The DL speaks as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November 2026. On Bluefen, Riverlark and especially the DD-006 incident, the position has almost certainly moved. We need an updated DL and current facts before signing.

---

## 2. Material issues and pushback

### A. Known liabilities must not be routed through warranties

The quantified known items are:

- Riverlark AUD 3.2m
- Bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs
- Ironquay AUD 180k
- Sandbar AUD 330k

That totals **about AUD 4.13m or more, roughly 86% of the AUD 4.8m cap.** These items are disclosed, so they would not be warranty claims at all. Even if they were, the basket, the cap and the 18-month limit would erode recovery.

**Principle for the mark-up:** Known issues are dealt with through price, conditions precedent (CPs) or specific indemnities, never through the general warranty regime.

### B. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): reject "release following Completion"

- The deal is **debt-free/cash-free**. The AUD 3.2m is Indebtedness and must be repaid **at** Completion out of the price, not afterwards.
- The facility has a change-control clause (8.1). Completion without a discharge risks an event of default or acceleration against a company we will by then own. The Riverlark security would also remain registered over the company's assets.
- **Ask for:**
  - Payout letter as a Completion deliverable, with a per-diem figure.
  - Direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow, deducted from the price.
  - Signed deed of release and discharge of all security.
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to file them, at Completion.
  - Confirmation that there is no security over the shares themselves; check this in the title diligence.
  - Debt definition to include break costs, fees and accrued interest.

### C. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): strengthen the CP

Bluefen is about **30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m)**. This is a deal-critical consent, and it has not been obtained.

- "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak. Ask for **all reasonable endeavours**, or best endeavours, with a duty to keep us informed and to let us participate in discussions with Bluefen.
- "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" is not enough. The CP should require:
  - written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, acting reasonably;
  - **evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**, or that those conditions are acceptable to the Buyer;
  - the consent not having been withdrawn, varied or made subject to new terms (such as pricing changes or termination rights) by Completion.
- The CP should be for the Buyer's benefit only, so that only we can waive it, with a sensible long-stop date.
- Add:
  - a warranty and a pre-Completion covenant that Bluefen has not given notice of termination or non-renewal, or indicated an intention to reduce volume;
  - a Buyer termination right if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces its business before Completion.
- Consider whether a price adjustment, retention or earn-out linked to Bluefen retention is warranted, given the dependence on one customer.

### D. Completion bonuses, AUD 420k (DD-005): put them in the funds flow

- The cover note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller". However, the **company** is the employer and legal obligor. After Completion that liability sits with us.
- Treat them as **Transaction Expenses / Indebtedness**, deducted from the price, **grossed up for employer on-costs**, including:
  - NSW payroll tax;
  - superannuation guarantee, where the bonus counts as ordinary time earnings (to be confirmed by tax and employment advisers);
  - workers' compensation premium and PAYG administration.
- Payment should go through payroll, with PAYG withholding.
- Where a bonus has a **post-Completion continued-employment condition**, the Seller should still fund it, for example through an amount retained or deducted at Completion. Any unvested amount that lapses can be released back to the Seller if we agree.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including on-costs and penalties, outside the cap and thresholds.

### E. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): the indemnity is the wrong shape

- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, **title to the SOW3 Project Materials only transfers once every SOW3 fee has cleared**. DD-010 shows AUD 180k still open, and payment has not been independently verified. The company may therefore **not own** IP that is likely core to an analytics business.
- An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" covers the wrong loss. The real exposure is ownership and infringement: rebuild costs, third-party claims, injunctions, and loss of the ability to licence or commercialise.
- **Ask for:**
  - A CP, or at least a Completion deliverable, that the outstanding SOW3 fees are paid at the Seller's cost (or deducted as Debt).
  - Evidence of cleared funds.
  - A **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay, plus moral rights consents from the individual developers.
  - A specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any defect in the company's title to, or right to use, the SOW3 materials, outside the general cap and thresholds.
  - IP warranties (ownership and non-infringement) treated as **enhanced**, with a higher cap and longer period than general warranties.

### F. DD-006 export and privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6): the most time-sensitive item

- The download link went to an unintended external address. About **1,240 records** of personal information may be affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, once an entity suspects an eligible data breach it must carry out a reasonable assessment, generally within **30 days**. If the assessment confirms an eligible data breach, it must notify the OAIC and affected individuals. The investigation was "preliminary" on 22 September. Six weeks later, **the company may already be outside that window**, and that is a compliance risk we would inherit.
- Customer contracts may also impose their own notification deadlines. Check this for Bluefen in particular. If Bluefen data is affected, this links back to Issue C.
- **Ask for, now:**
  - the incident timeline, including the date the company became aware;
  - any forensic or IT report;
  - link access logs, if available;
  - the outcome of the eligible-data-breach assessment;
  - copies of any notifications made;
  - insurer notification under any cyber policy.
- **In the SPA:**
  - a specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the incident, including investigation, notification, remediation, customer claims, credits, regulatory costs and defence costs, outside the cap and thresholds. Note that indemnity for civil penalties may be unenforceable as a matter of public policy, so draft it to the extent permitted by law.
  - a pre-Completion covenant that the incident is handled in consultation with us;
  - a warranty that there are no other incidents.
- If the facts deteriorate, keep the option of a Completion CP or a termination right.

### G. Fundamental, title and tax warranties: reject "same caps and time limits"

- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to put **title and capacity** at 20% and 18 months. If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing.
  - **Cap:** 100% of the price.
  - **Time limit:** at least 6 years, matching the NSW contract limitation period, or longer if the SPA is executed as a deed.
  - **Thresholds:** none.
- **Tax:** the Seller says this is "settled under the general regime". It is not. We need a **separate tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax:
  - capped at 100% of the price;
  - with a time limit tied to the ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods, typically 4–5 years plus a margin (often 7 years in total), and unlimited for fraud or evasion;
  - with no de minimis or basket.
- **Title verification:** DD-012 is just the company's own register. DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified it. We need:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates and allotment and transfer history;
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, SAFEs or ESOP entitlements, which is especially relevant for a VC-backed company;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - if Harbourglass holds the shares as trustee of a fund, the trust deed and evidence of trustee power, plus trustee capacity warranties.

### H. Disclosure standard (DL 1.1–1.2, Sch 7): limit to fair, specific disclosure

- **Strike general disclosure of the data room and public registers.** Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the DL itself should qualify the warranties. "Fairly disclosed" means with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and approximate financial effect.
- Fallback, if we must concede something: specific data room documents only, listed by DD number, from a fixed USB copy, and still subject to the fair-disclosure standard. Never "every fact, matter or circumstance… referred to".
- Public records: at most, the results of searches of specific named registers, obtained on a stated date.
- DL 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if the SPA says it does not limit any indemnity, CP or price mechanism.
- There should be **no updating of the DL between signing and Completion to cure breaches.** New matters should give us a claim, or a termination right if material.

### I. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): delete it

- "Knowledge… including any matter discoverable" by us "or our advisers" combined with full data room disclosure would bar nearly everything.
- Replace it with a pro-buyer clause: the Buyer's rights are **not affected by any knowledge or investigation**, other than matters fairly disclosed in the DL.

### J. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): carve-outs needed

Apply these to **general warranty claims only**. Carve out:

- **fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** by the Seller, the company or their agents, in which case no limitation applies;
- specific indemnities, tax and fundamental warranties (with their own regimes);
- price adjustment, leakage, Debt and Transaction Expense mechanics;
- termination, specific performance and injunctive relief.

The 18-month limit should apply only to general warranties, and expressly so. The Seller's proposal that limitations apply to everything "unless expressly stated otherwise" puts the drafting burden in the wrong place.

### K. Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1 / 12.2)

- **Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** within market range for general warranties if everything else in this memo is fixed. Open at 30–35% and use it as a trade-off.
- **De minimis AUD 25k:** acceptable-ish, but seek AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
- **Basket AUD 250k (about 1.04%) as a deductible:** push for a **tipping basket**, so that once it is exceeded we recover from the first dollar. Accept a lower deductible only as a trade.
- **Credit support:** the Seller is a venture vehicle that may distribute the proceeds. Seek a **retention or escrow**, for example 10–15% of the price for 18 months, or a parent or fund guarantee. If W&I insurance is being considered, the cap, threshold and retention structure changes, and we should decide that early. Note also that W&I will exclude known issues such as Items B–F and L.

### L. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k, DD-008 / DD-011)

- Three renewals of exactly AUD 110k with "related" timing and scope suggest the contract may have been **split to stay under an approval or conduct-of-business threshold**. The DL deliberately does not say they are ordinary course.
- **Ask for:**
  - dates and terms of each renewal;
  - whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller;
  - whether the commitments are terminable, prepaid or accrued in working capital;
  - confirmation they were entered in compliance with any existing restrictions.
- If any were entered after the locked-box or accounts date, or outside the ordinary course, treat them as **leakage** or a price adjustment.
- Add pre-Completion covenants that aggregate related contracts when applying approval thresholds.

### M. Lower-priority items to confirm

- **Office lease (DD-007):** confirm the notification has been or will be given on time. Check whether the lease deems a change in control to be an assignment.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** confirm there is no deemed-assignment or change-of-control trigger. Ask for a warranty that the share sale does not breach or trigger rights under any material contract.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay at Completion from price; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharge as deliverables |
| 2 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent suffices | All reasonable endeavours; Buyer-satisfactory consent including 11.3 conditions; Buyer-only waiver; termination right |
| 3 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Expense, grossed up for payroll tax, super and on-costs; specific indemnity |
| 4 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Pay fees at Seller cost; confirmatory assignment as deliverable; full title and IP indemnity outside cap |
| 5 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Urgent update on NDB assessment status; specific indemnity outside cap; conduct covenant; possible CP |
| 6 | Title, capacity, tax | General cap and 18 months | 100% cap, 6+ years; separate tax indemnity; independent title verification |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure in DL only; updated DL; no curative updates before Completion |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Knowledge or discoverability bars claims | Delete; knowledge does not affect rights |
| 9 | Limitations and non-reliance | Apply to all Claims | General warranties only; carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, fundamentals, price mechanics, equitable relief |
| 10 | Cap and thresholds | 20%, AUD 25k, AUD 250k deductible | Seek 30–35%; AUD 10–15k; tipping basket; escrow or guarantee |
| 11 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Full information; leakage or price adjustment if not ordinary course; aggregate related contracts |
| 12 | Lease, Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify; no-conflict warranty |

**Immediate actions, before the mark-up goes back:**

1. Request current status on DD-006 (NDB assessment and notifications), Bluefen and Riverlark, and an updated DL dated near signing.
2. Commission independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, cap table and any trust structure) and evidence of Ironquay payment.
3. Ask the financial and tax advisers to quantify bonus on-costs and the Debt and Transaction Expense deductions for the funds flow.
4. Decide on W&I insurance versus a Seller escrow, because it shapes the cap and threshold negotiation.

These positions are for discussion with the deal team and NSW counsel. Final positions should reflect the full SPA text, the data room documents and the commercial priorities.

  - a specific indemnity for all Loss arising from the incident, including investigation, notification, remediation, customer claims, credits, regulatory costs and defence costs, outside the cap and thresholds. Note that indemnity for civil penalties may be unenforceable as a matter of public policy, so draft it to the extent permitted by law.
  - a pre-Completion covenant that the incident is handled in consultation with us;
  - a warranty that there are no other incidents.
- If the facts deteriorate, keep the option of a Completion CP or a termination right.

### G. Fundamental, title and tax warranties: reject "same caps and time limits"

- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to put **title and capacity** at 20% and 18 months. If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing.
  - **Cap:** 100% of the price.
  - **Time limit:** at least 6 years, matching the NSW contract limitation period, or longer if the SPA is executed as a deed.
  - **Thresholds:** none.
- **Tax:** the Seller says this is "settled under the general regime". It is not. We need a **separate tax indemnity** for pre-Completion tax:
  - capped at 100% of the price;
  - with a time limit tied to the ATO and Revenue NSW amendment periods, typically 4–5 years plus a margin (often 7 years in total), and unlimited for fraud or evasion;
  - with no de minimis or basket.
- **Title verification:** DD-012 is just the company's own register. DL 10 itself says the Buyer has not verified it. We need:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates and allotment and transfer history;
  - confirmation that there are no options, convertibles, SAFEs or ESOP entitlements, which is especially relevant for a VC-backed company;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - if Harbourglass holds the shares as trustee of a fund, the trust deed and evidence of trustee power, plus trustee capacity warranties.

### H. Disclosure standard (DL 1.1–1.2, Sch 7): limit to fair, specific disclosure

- **Strike general disclosure of the data room and public registers.** Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the DL itself should qualify the warranties. "Fairly disclosed" means with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and approximate financial effect.
- Fallback, if we must concede something: specific data room documents only, listed by DD number, from a fixed USB copy, and still subject to the fair-disclosure standard. Never "every fact, matter or circumstance… referred to".
- Public records: at most, the results of searches of specific named registers, obtained on a stated date.
- DL 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if the SPA says it does not limit any indemnity, CP or price mechanism.
- There should be **no updating of the DL between signing and Completion to cure breaches.** New matters should give us a claim, or a termination right if material.

### I. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): delete it

- "Knowledge… including any matter discoverable" by us "or our advisers" combined with full data room disclosure would bar nearly everything.
- Replace it with a pro-buyer clause: the Buyer's rights are **not affected by any knowledge or investigation**, other than matters fairly disclosed in the DL.

### J. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): carve-outs needed

Apply these to **general warranty claims only**. Carve out:

- **fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** by the Seller, the company or their agents, in which case no limitation applies;
- specific indemnities, tax and fundamental warranties (with their own regimes);
- price adjustment, leakage, Debt and Transaction Expense mechanics;
- termination, specific performance and injunctive relief.

The 18-month limit should apply only to general warranties, and expressly so. The Seller's proposal that limitations apply to everything "unless expressly stated otherwise" puts the drafting burden in the wrong place.

### K. Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1 / 12.2)

- **Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** within market range for general warranties if everything else in this memo is fixed. Open at 30–35% and use it as a trade-off.
- **De minimis AUD 25k:** acceptable-ish, but seek AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
- **Basket AUD 250k (about 1.04%) as a deductible:** push for a **tipping basket**, so that once it is exceeded we recover from the first dollar. Accept a lower deductible only as a trade.
- **Credit support:** the Seller is a venture vehicle that may distribute the proceeds. Seek a **retention or escrow**, for example 10–15% of the price for 18 months, or a parent or fund guarantee. If W&I insurance is being considered, the cap, threshold and retention structure changes, and we should decide that early. Note also that W&I will exclude known issues such as Items B–F and L.

### L. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k, DD-008 / DD-011)

- Three renewals of exactly AUD 110k with "related" timing and scope suggest the contract may have been **split to stay under an approval or conduct-of-business threshold**. The DL deliberately does not say they are ordinary course.
- **Ask for:**
  - dates and terms of each renewal;
  - whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller;
  - whether the commitments are terminable, prepaid or accrued in working capital;
  - confirmation they were entered in compliance with any existing restrictions.
- If any were entered after the locked-box or accounts date, or outside the ordinary course, treat them as **leakage** or a price adjustment.
- Add pre-Completion covenants that aggregate related contracts when applying approval thresholds.

### M. Lower-priority items to confirm

- **Office lease (DD-007):** confirm the notification has been or will be given on time. Check whether the lease deems a change in control to be an assignment.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** confirm there is no deemed-assignment or change-of-control trigger. Ask for a warranty that the share sale does not breach or trigger rights under any material contract.
